meta.title: HISD, Fort Worth ISD and state takeovers, 18 days of posts
meta.subject: school district governance and state intervention in Texas — HISD under the TEA-appointed board of managers and Superintendent Mike Miles, Fort Worth ISD and other TEA takeovers, the return to elected boards, trustee redistricting, SB 1882 partnerships, A-F ratings used as justification, and the campaign for and against the reforms
meta.subtitle: Oct 1 to Oct 18, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about HISD, Fort Worth ISD and Texas school takeovers, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Takeover is a proven turnaround
lanes.description: The state takeover and Miles' reforms are working, citing improved A-F ratings, rising achievement, 'largest turnaround in Texas history', 'no student attends a failing school', and a financially sustainable model.

lanes.label: Undemocratic state power grab
lanes.description: The takeover strips local voters and parents of control, with Abbott, Morath and TEA hand-picking unaccountable managers and a commission report offering a counternarrative to the state's account; the fix is returning to an elected board.

lanes.label: Harm to classrooms and staff
lanes.description: Reforms have damaged schools through scripted lessons, narrowed curriculum, cut arts programs, teacher turnover, harsh discipline, school closures and bus hub changes, as voiced by students and parents.

lanes.label: Money, enrollment and vouchers
lanes.description: Funding and enrollment losses, voucher diversion, surplus spending and school closures show the state's priorities hurting neighborhood schools and costing taxpayers.

lanes.label: Fort Worth as the next HISD
lanes.description: Fort Worth ISD's takeover is repeating the Houston model, with Board of Managers meetings, student pushback and a warning that other districts are next.

lanes.label: Privatization, edtech and election politics
lanes.description: The takeover is framed as serving tech and private interests (Alpha School, TimeBack, SB 1882 partners) and as a campaign issue for the governor's race and November ballot.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.
